reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Poisson.Compensated.stageErr
Standing setting (paper section 2, intro (eq:mvfbsdej), section 3 solution space, section 4,
appendix A): (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0; a d-dim
Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity
dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, calE); (F_t) is the usual augmentation
of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial sigma-field F_0. The compensated
measure is Ntilde(dt,de) = N(dt,de) - dt nu(de). Integrands U of the Poisson integral are
predictable: P (x) calE-measurable, P the predictable sigma-field on Omega x [0,T]
(eq:fubiniiso), with E int_0^T ||U_t||^2_{L2(nu)} dt < infinity (the space H^2_N). The
integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) is the standard L2 (Ito-Levy) compensated-Poisson
integral: an L2 martingale, cadlag, with the isometry E|int_0^t int U dNtilde|^2 =
E int_0^t ||U_s||^2 ds (used in Lemma 4.1 "true L2-martingales by the Ito and
compensated-Poisson isometries"), jumps Delta = U_s(e) at atoms (s,e) of N, and for integrands
in L1(dP dt nu) the integral splits as int U dN - int U nu ds (eq:compid, eq:zeromean).
Progressive measurability is used for the coefficient processes b, sigma, f and the forcings
q^b, q^sigma, q^f (eq:coefmeas, section 4); predictability (P (x) calE) for h and q^h.

Reading.
The paper uses only the finished integral int_0^t int_E U_s(e) Ntilde(ds,de) for U in H^2_N
(predictable, P (x) calE-measurable, E int_0^T ||U_s||^2 ds < infinity), with the standard
properties: for each t it is the L2(Omega)-limit of elementary integrals of step integrands
approximating U in H^2_N (the isometric extension, independent of the approximating sequence);
the process t -> int_0^t is taken in a cadlag version (the paper uses its jumps, running suprema
via Doob/BDG, and "both sides of each identity are cadlag in t"), an (F_t) square-integrable
martingale, determined up to indistinguishability. Any construction of it (staged
approximations, horizon-by-horizon pieces, a.s.-convergent fast subsequences, a "master"
cadlag limit) is an implementation choice of layer 2. An auxiliary of the construction is
faithful when it is a correct step towards a final integral with these properties, and no junk
value of it (a default for non-integrable U, a limit taken where the sequence does not converge,
a toReal of infinity) reaches the integral on the class of integrands the propositions use;
outside H^2_N (or on non-predictable U) any junk value is harmless provided every proposition
using the integral imposes membership in H^2_N on its integrands (as the paper does: U in H^2_N,
h along a solution in L2).

Specific to stageErr: presumably the approximation error at stage n (distance in H^2_N between
U, possibly truncated to a horizon, and its n-th step approximation, or the L2 distance between
consecutive stage integrals), used to choose a fast subsequence so that the stage integrals
converge a.s. uniformly in t. Faithful if it is a correct error quantity of that kind (an ENNReal
or real number that tends to 0 for U in H^2_N), so that the selection it drives is legitimate;
its value never enters a proposition directly.

comparison.text:
Lean construction (LevyStochCalc/Poisson/CompensatedApprox.lean, CompensatedProcess.lean,
Compensated.lean). Common parameters: N : PoissonRandomMeasure P nu (nu sigma-finite, P a
probability), F : Filtration R, hF : IsPoissonFiltration N F, phi : Omega -> R -> E -> R with
h_meas (joint measurability on Omega x R x E), h_progMeas (MarkedProgressivelyMeasurable F phi)
and h_sq_int_global (for every T > 0, E int_{[0,T]} int_E |phi|^2 dnu ds < infinity). All
integrability/measurability conditions are explicit arguments, so there is no junk value for an
inadmissible integrand: the objects are simply not defined for it. Chain: stageHorizon n = 2^n;
exists_stage gives an Adapted MarkStep on a dyadic grid of [0,2^n] of level >= L0 within
1/(n+1) of phi in L2(P x ds x nu) on [0,2^n] (stageErr); master n chooses these with levels
strictly increasing (master_level_succ); stageIntegral n t = (master n).2.integral N t (an
F-martingale, in L2, zero for t <= 0); stageLp t n = its L2(P) class; stageLp_cauchySeq proves
the sequence Cauchy in L2(P) for every t (via the L2 distance bound stageIntegral_sub_sq_le and
Doob monotonicity of second moments), so processLp t = limUnder atTop (stageLp t) is the true
limit (stageLp_tendsto); process t = an F_t-measurable representative of processLp t;
stochasticIntegral = Classical.choose of exists_cadlag_modification: an F.rightCont-adapted,
a.s. cadlag (right limits = value, left limits exist, for all t simultaneously a.s.) process with
stochasticIntegral t = process t a.s. for every t. Proved properties: martingale for F.rightCont,
isometry E|I_T|^2 = E int_{[0,T]} int_E |phi|^2 (isometry_stochasticIntegral), compensated square
a martingale, difference isometry.
Why this is the paper integral on the paper class: on adapted step integrands the stage integral
is the paper elementary integral (MarkStep.integral). For a predictable (P (x) calE-measurable)
square-integrable phi - which is MarkedProgressivelyMeasurable and jointly measurable
(MarkedPredictable.markedProgressivelyMeasurable, markedPredictableSigma_le) - the approximants
converge to phi in L2(P x ds x nu), so by the isometry their integrals converge in L2(P) to the
isometric extension of the elementary integral, which is the paper L2 integral (the limit does
not depend on the approximating sequence, by the isometry). Hence processLp t is the paper
integral up to t as an L2 class, process t a version of it, and stochasticIntegral its cadlag
version, unique up to indistinguishability.
Specific to stageErr P n G: the ENNReal L2 error int_omega int_{Icc 0 (2^n)} int_E
|phi - G.eval|^2 dnu ds dP of a mark-step integrand on the stage-n grid against phi, on the
stage-n horizon. It drives the choice in master (< 1/(n+1)); it tends to 0 along master. A
correct error quantity; never enters a proposition directly. Matches the reading.
